title: La Rocca's left-handed cornet and his heart condition
summary: He explains the cornet was a 1920 gift, is left-handed, and that heart trouble now stops him playing except at home.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well you see this instrument, I bought it and I didn't buy it, it was given to me as a present.
How long have you gone, Mr. Martin?

This would be in 1920. This was given to me. I think it's the only left hand instrument, that is, you'll see a sign up at the Tulane, they have a big photograph of a bushy instrument. This is a bushy, see your finger, this is from the left. Now in the ordinary they play from the right. Don't ask me to blow it because I have heart trouble and I'm not supposed to blow on the instrument anymore. Not drink, nothing.
How long did you have played?
Well, before I had this last heart attack I used to sit down and blow a little bit.
Just for myself, yeah, you know, just to sit around and blow a little bit on it.
